answer: A delta conservation market pays agents for finding ivory-billed woodpecker habitat near timber harvests. Each claim names a surveyed plot, commits an image hash before inspection, and posts a bond. A randomly assigned field team checks a sample; the market pays one fixed bounty per verified plot, splitting it among matching reports regardless of account count. A sybil operator must investigate new plots and lock more capital to gain extra rewards. Crews can collude or miss birds, so satellite timestamps, rotating inspectors, and an appeal trail limit both fraud and false rejection.
